reaction: The result matched what I expected.

expectation: The vessels will be arranged beside the receiving cells.

effect: The channels are fitted, and their local openings pass an electrical change along the fibre. The remaining goal is to join the two prepared parts.
reaction: The distinction between a travelling electrical change and an ion travelling the whole length was interesting.
reason: The supplied cell bodies and channel-bearing fibres match the parts named in the new goal.
expectation: The fibres will join the receiving cells and their blood supply to form nervous tissue.

effect: The prepared cells and fibres joined into nervous tissue, completing the chapter; the vessels supply the living cells with food and oxygen.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two projects come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the channels was most worthwhile: the picture explained how local changes pass a signal along a fibre without one ion travelling the whole way.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the blood vessels was clear but fairly predictable; it mostly confirmed that the cells need food and oxygen.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the electrical change travels along the fibre through neighbouring channels opening, rather than a single ion travelling its full length.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary: each pairing followed a named goal and the pictures explained its purpose.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see what the nervous tissue connects to next; the explanation of how the signal travels made me curious.
